annotations.text:
BUILT — Option B, chosen by Ash.

Four of the five controls moved onto the rows whose values they change. Only Block keeps the foot: it is the one thing here that takes something away from a person rather than adjusting a setting about them, and it has no fact-row of its own to sit on.

Choosing this settled the open question: the Referring row is now drawn ALWAYS, reading Active or Stopped, where before it appeared only once referring had been stopped. A switch that materialises the first time you use it is worse than the drawer it replaced.

Kept as the record of the decision, not as live work.

The left board is what shipped in §116 and what was reported as "not clear". A and C were the alternatives; neither was taken.
